analysis.title: Record Shorts, Record Buybacks...
key_insights: NDX remains in the same range it has held since May. Chasing momentum at either range extreme has continued to lose money for traders.

GS PB data shows short sales outpacing long buying 5:1 month-to-date, pushing short leverage close to five-year highs while NDX has not broken its range. The Market Ear frames this as potential fuel for an upside squeeze.
The GS buyback desk estimates 12% of the S&P 500 is in an open buyback window today, with 22% exiting blackout by the end of the week.
GS's Ranganath desk reports 2026 YTD buyback authorizations at a record $1,305bn, versus $1,151bn in 2025 and prior peaks of $959bn (2022) and $951bn (2024).
Russell 2000 is trading around a trendline that has held since May 2025. It is below its 200-day moving average, as it was in March before it bounced sharply.
Russell is sensitive to rising yields. As the 10-year yield has paused, the RUT/NDX ratio has caught a bid and the spread reversed off the lower part of its trend line.

JPMorgan data shows Samsung, SK Hynix and Micron down an average 42% from recent peaks, against an average drawdown of about 49% in the previous four major memory downcycles. JPMorgan sees little evidence that a downturn has begun.
The market appears to be discounting a memory earnings peak as early as 1H 2027. Samsung and SK Hynix trade at 2-3x estimated 2027/2028 earnings and about 0.9-1.5x forward price-to-book (GS).
Since Brazil's first-round election, EWZ options flows have turned defensive, pushing near-term skew to record highs (GS).

French OAT spreads have widened sharply, but Italian and Greek spreads versus Germany have narrowed this month. Authers (Bloomberg) says investors are treating France as an isolated sovereign problem, unlike 2010-12. The note cautions that France's place in Europe's core makes broader contagion possible.

sector_views.rationale: JPMorgan sees little evidence a memory downturn has begun, though the stocks have already fallen about 42% on average, close to the 49% average in past downcycles.

earnings_insights: Samsung and SK Hynix trade at 2-3x estimated 2027/2028 earnings (GS), pricing in a memory earnings peak as early as 1H 2027.

macro_indicators.interpretation: A record, above $1,151bn in 2025 and the prior peaks of $959bn (2022) and $951bn (2024). It points to corporate buying support into year-end.

risk_factors: A sharp memory earnings reversal could validate the current discount in Samsung, SK Hynix and Micron.
Brazil's election outcome adds downside risk, as reflected in record EWZ skew.
French sovereign stress could spread to the rest of Europe's core.

tension_points.bear_case: NDX has stayed trapped in its range since May, and chasing momentum at the highs has been punished.

tension_points.bull_case: The three stocks are down an average 42% against a 49% average in past downcycles. JPMorgan sees little evidence a downturn has begun, and Samsung and SK Hynix trade at 2-3x 2027/2028 earnings.
